page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-1xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server configured with 16 vCPUs and 192 GB of system memory, running on the KVM hypervisor. The processing core is powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor based on the x86_64 architecture, featuring 16 physical cores with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared. For acceleration, the server integrates a single NVIDIA L40S GPU from the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 48 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier single-core and multi-core capabilities. The server achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2959.0 and a multi-core score of 22269.0, both placing in the top 10% tier. In stress-ng testing, single-core performance reached 4172.89 (top 10%), while multi-core performance registered at 67220.77 (top 25%). Memory bandwidth is strong, with large-block read-only speeds at 329.44 GB/sec and write speeds at 143.42 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the system demonstrates top-tier performance in image processing (21321.0) and text processing (4233.0), alongside strong database operations (22382.01) and Redis SET throughput at 67.91 million operations per second.

The hardware configuration is optimized for machine learning and artificial intelligence workloads. In LLM inference benchmarks using a small 135M model, the server delivers top-tier prompt processing at 3898.64 tokens per second and text generation at 386.1 tokens per second. For medium 7B models, text generation remains strong at 36.41 tokens per second, while larger 70B models run at average speeds of 3.88 tokens per second for generation. These metrics indicate suitability for AI model inference, data science, image processing, and database operations. The shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage represent key architectural tradeoffs to consider for sustained high-compute workloads.
